Our diversity embodies the understanding that each individual is unique, and recognizes our individual differences. medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Chicago Medical School at Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science is situated in the northern suburbs of Chicago, with easy access to downtown Chicago and the surrounding areas by car or public transportation. State-of-the-art facilities include a $10 million research wing expansion, The Morningstar Interprofessional Education Center, The Rothstein Warden Centennial Learning Center, a gross anatomy laboratory and classrooms fully-equipped for multimedia-enhanced learning, and the Education and Evaluation Center for physical examination skills training. Recreational facilities include a brand new fitness center, game room, and the brand-new Student Union (home to the University Bookstore, Union Cafe, and computer lab).  For more information about our facilities, please visit the following website:
https://www.rosalindfranklin.edu/academics/facilities/
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
On-campus housing is available at Rosalind Franklin University. The University's three residential buildings offer one and two-bedroom apartments. Each on-campus apartment building includes study and lounge areas, shared laundry facilities on every floor and individual storage units. For information on student housing, please visit the following website: https://rosalindfranklin.edu/campus-life/student-housing/on-campus-housing/

Rosalind Franklin University has partnered with The Woodlands on Green Bay Apartment Community to offer an off-campus housing option reserved exclusively for students at the University. The Woodlands on Green Bay offers one and two bedroom apartments.https://www.rosalindfranklin.edu/campus-life/student-housing/woodlands-apartments/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Rosalind Franklin University supports and fosters an inclusive campus community. For more information visit the Diversity & Inclusion website: https://www.rosalindfranklin.edu/about/strategic-initiatives/diversity-inclusion/.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: In addition to faculty office hours, RFUMS offers a variety of tutoring options for students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Clinical foundations of medicine (CFOM), M1 & M2 ECR and sophomore electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures deliver curricular content along with case-based discussions enriched with eight curricular threads, laboratories, workshops, simulation exercises and standardized patient experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Internal medicine, surgery, obstetrics/gynecology, pediatrics, family medicine, psychiatry, and neurology
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Not required unless specified in the course syllabus
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: In 2018, Chicago Medical School (CMS) implemented a revised curriculum which is delivered in three phases. Phase I (M1/M2 yrs.) addresses the foundational knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behaviors of a physician and emphasizes clinically relevant educational experiences. Phase II (M3 yr.) builds on the knowledge and skills of Phase I by providing seven core clerkships and one elective experience for career exploration. Phase III (M4 yr.) allows students to deepen their understanding of medical specialties in preparation for residency training.  CMS is one of six graduate health and sciences colleges at RFUMS, which allows for team-based, interprofessional learning and practice opportunities devoted to defining roles and fostering teamwork. This continues throughout the curriculum via service learning, global health, simulation, and patient care experiences.  As a community-based medical school, CMS has a diverse set of affiliate sites providing students with rich and varied clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
There is a lot of research at RFUMS, in both the clinical and basic sciences. Our basic sciences strengths include neuroscience, physiology, structural biology, cancer, and regenerative medicine. Research fellowships are available for students during the summer between M1 and M2 years, and there is also an opportunity to continue research during elective time in years 2, 3 and 4. For several students each year, this work leads to graduation with an "MD with a Distinction in Research" certificate. For students who wish to pursue a combined MD/PhD degree, two tracks are available. 

For more information about Rosalind Franklin University's research opportunities, please visit the following website:  https://www.rosalindfranklin.edu/academics/school-of-graduate-and-postdoctoral-studies/degree-programs/

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded in 1912, The Chicago Medical School has been dedicated to excellence in medical education for over a century. The Chicago Medical School has educated thousands of professionals with recognized innovation in health education, excellence in the creation of knowledge and scientific discovery focused on prediction and prevention of disease, outstanding clinical programs, and compassionate community service. For a list of our major hospital affiliates you may visit: https://www.rosalindfranklin.edu/academics/chicago-medical-school/degree-programs/allopathic-medicine-md/rotations/
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Chicago Medical School’s mission is to educate a diverse student body in a community-engaged, interprofessional environment. Our graduates become exemplary, compassionate physicians and scientists dedicated to improving the health and wellness of their patients and communities through clinical excellence, scientific discovery, service, and leadership.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
What are the important 2026-2027 Choose Your Medical School (CYMS) dates for the Chicago Medical School (CMS)? 

April 30, 2027 – Incoming CMS students can begin to indicate “commit to enroll” using the AMCAS CYMS tool. 

June 15, 2027 – All incoming CMS students are required to indicate “commit to enroll” using the AMCAS CYMS tool. Failure to meet this deadline could result in your offer of admission being withdrawn by the Student Admissions Committee. 

Chicago Medical School - Academic Work Affected by the COVID-19 Outbreak 

Pass/Fail Grades: 
CMS will accept pass/no pass grades, without prejudice, for courses taken during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

Online Coursework: 
CMS will accept online coursework including labs recognized and verified by AMCAS, without prejudice for courses taken during the COVID-19 pandemic.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The Chicago Medical School maintains a strong institutional commitment to equal educational opportunities for academically prepared students. The following technical standards are requirements for admission, progression and graduation and are intended to welcome all candidates and ensure that candidates for admission are able to complete the entire course of study and participate fully in all aspects of medical training. Technical standards may be met with or without reasonable accommodations. The Chicago Medical School is committed to the full and equitable inclusion of qualified learners with disabilities. If you are an applicant with a disability who may require accommodations in our program, confidentially contact the ADA Coordinator at 847.578.8354 or ada.coordinator@rosalindfranklin.edu. Requests for academic accommodations are reviewed by the ADA Coordinator in the University Division of Student Success and Wellness to determine if there are reasonable accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy:
TUITION AND FEE PAYMENT POLICY 
All students will pay full tuition for 14 quarters. 

Tuition and fees are due 6 business days prior to the term begin date, regardless of when classes actually start. Beginning on the first day of each term, a a late assessment fee calculated on a daily basis at the rate of 18% per annum is assessed to each student's account which is not yet paid. 

Failure to pay tuition and fees in full by the end of the academic term will result in a student not being 
allowed to register for the subsequent term.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Students in the Chicago Medical School (CMS) are able to earn combined MD/PhD degrees by application to the School of Graduate of Postdoctoral Studies after matriculation into CMS.
Please visiting the following website: https://rosalindfranklin.edu/academics/school-of-graduate-and-postdoctoral-studies/

Pre-matriculation Program (PMP) is a multi-track academic enrichment program. PMP offers highly motivated post-baccalaureate students from disadvantaged backgrounds the opportunity to enroll at no cost in a non-degree curriculum track. These tracks give students the ability to experience medical school level coursework while preparing to take or re-take the MCAT and grants additional, competitive academic development and experience to students seeking to improve their competitiveness as a medical or health professions degree applicant.

Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences (BMS) program will prepare you to continue your graduate education in a variety of healthcare professions. This academic enhancement program provides a rigorous background in the biomedical sciences in a challenging one-year course of study and the opportunity to interact with students in other health profession degree programs.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Required Coursework
•1 year Introductory Biology w/ laboratory (*or equivalent)
•1 year Physics w/ laboratory
•2 years Chemistry sequence including all 3 of disciplines below:
-General/Inorganic Chemistry w/ laboratory
-Organic Chemistry w/ laboratory
-Biochemistry (laboratory recommended)
•2 courses in Behavioral/Social Sciences (Introductory courses in  Psychology and Sociology courses strongly suggested)

* We encourage research laboratory experience either through research or lab research course.

RECOMMENDED COURSES

•1 course in Statistics
•1 course in Advanced Biology (200 level or above; e.g., Molecular and Cell Biology, Physiology, Genetics, Microbiology, Neurobiology)
•English composition
•Other coursework in the Humanities and Social Sciences

CMS requires  at least 90 hours of undergraduate academic coursework at an accredited college or university prior to applying.

The vast majority of successful applicants have earned a Bachelor's degree prior to enrollment.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have an expiration date on when coursework can be completed.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
CMS uses a holistic approach in evaluating applications, emphasizing a range of factors including medical, humanitarian, research, employment, leadership, and other varied life experiences. We seek students who understand the dynamics of healthcare teams and the role of a physician within that team, often demonstrated through prior employment and volunteer/community work.

We also value candidates who are committed to serving others and have shown leadership potential through academic, research, or other endeavors. In addition, we look for students who exhibit a caring attitude and strong interpersonal communication skills.

Each application is evaluated based on academic achievement,  letters of recommendation, personal interviews, and experiences. To fulfill the mission of CMS, our admissions policies are designed to ensure that we select individuals who are dedicated to providing exemplary, compassionate patient care.
